title: BioLLMAgent: A Hybrid Framework with Enhanced Structural Interpretability for Simulating Human Decision-Making in Computational Psychiatry

model.params_source: paper Sec. IV.A (T = 0.5, top-p 0.9, gpt-4o-2024-05-13); max_tokens assumed

task.subset_rule: 30 independent calls (simulated participants) per seed; from each returned distribution 100 deck choices are sampled with a fixed RNG (seed 20260907), giving 3,000 pooled choices (resolution plan budget)
task.approximation: the number of simulated participants/trials behind Table V is unstated; the LLM-only prior is evaluated without the ORL/PyMC loop; KL scales with sample size, so KL <= 0.01 is treated as agreement

items.source: Appendix A.1 Neutral Prior Prompt (the prompt is the whole input; no dataset)

prompt.system: You are an agent participating in a decision-making experiment called the Iowa Gambling Task.
prompt.user_template:
[Task]: You will make repeated choices from four card decks (A, B, C, D) over 100 trials. Each choice yields a monetary outcome (gain or loss). Your goal is to maximize total earnings.
[Instruction]: You have no prior information about the decks. Please select uniformly among the four options. Do not attempt to identify patterns or learn from previous outcomes—maintain uniform random selection throughout.
[Output]: Provide a probability distribution: {A: p_A, B: p_B, C: p_C, D: p_D}, where sum p = 1.0.
prompt.verbatim: full ([System] block sent as the system message; [Task]/[Instruction]/[Output] blocks as the user message with their labels; the extraction's 'P p= 1.0' rendered as 'sum p = 1.0')

output.postprocess: invalid or non-normalizable replies dropped and reported; 100 deck choices sampled from each valid distribution
output.parse_prose: regex the four probabilities 'A: p, B: p, C: p, D: p' (accept JSON or the braces format); normalize to sum 1

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: KL divergence KL(p_hat || uniform) = sum_d p_hat(d) log(p_hat(d)/0.25) over the pooled 3,000 sampled choices; also chi-square goodness-of-fit p-value against uniform and the standard deviation of the four deck proportions (Table V columns)
metric.original_location: Table V, row GPT-4o w/ (Chi-sq p 0.988, KL 0.002, Std 0.017)

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare 2026-09-07: est_usd_prepare counts <=400 output tokens per free-text call (runner out_guess); est_usd_dryrun_max_tokens counts the full max_tokens

notes: Because the prompt asks for a distribution rather than a choice, the pooled distribution can also be computed directly as the mean of the returned probabilities (no sampling); report both. The 'w/o' row (KL 0.124) drops the uniform-selection instruction sentence. || [hook 2026-09-07] parse() reads the four deck probabilities and normalises them; score() samples 100 choices per valid reply (seed 20260907), pools them and returns KL(p_hat || uniform); chi-square p (df 3, closed form), std of deck shares and the KL of the mean distribution are printed. No item-level CI (distribution-level metric).
